note: Held-out set drawn 2026-09-17 for the retrieval changes of section 12e (M11) of docs/plans/2026-09-17-006-what-twelve-reviews-found.md: the exhibit type read from the filing rather than from the filename, the coverage predicate, and filing selection by the quarters asked. It exists because the diagnosis that produced those changes was made on seed/cases/holdout_2026_09.json and on the runs behind it, and under rule 4 neither may score the fix for what it found. Every issuer here is absent from every other answer key under seed/, derived through tests/answer_keys.spent_issuers rather than checked against a list, and from the set drawn in parallel for the judging changes. What spends it: the first change measured on it. After that it is an oracle like the rest, and the next scored change needs a new set from issuers this file does not name. What each issuer is here for. Amphastar: an acquired product whose only pre-acquisition quarter is exhibit 99.2 of an 8-K/A under item 9.01, and a fourth quarter that is the annual row less the nine-month row. Pacira: a filing agent that names earnings exhibits pcrx-12312025x991.htm, with no ex99 in the name, so the shipped filename rule finds no earnings exhibit for the issuer and every fourth quarter is lost. Puma: the other naming convention, ex_973970.htm, and an issuer whose XBRL instance carries no quarterly product revenue under a product member at all, so the instance answers nothing and the exhibit is the only document that names the product beside a figure. Rigel: product detail that is in no periodic report - one total product sales line in the 10-Q, no quarterly product-sales fact under any product member in the instance, and every per-product figure a sentence in the 8-K EX-99.1. Both answers are here: quarters that carry a figure, a quarter whose acquisition closed on its last day, a quarter before the issuer took a product over, and a product licensed in after every quarter asked for. No case states a CIK on purpose: seed/example_drugs.csv has no such column, a person uploading a product types a ticker, and a case that stated one would hand the pipeline the issuer resolution this set is drawn to score.

cases.source: The acquirer bought the product from a filer that reports it inside a much larger portfolio, and the only statement of the product's own pre-acquisition sales is exhibit 99.2 of the acquirer's 8-K/A - unaudited abbreviated statements of revenues and direct expenses for the product line. After the acquisition the product is a row in the acquirer's segment table, and the fourth quarter of the year of acquisition is printed nowhere: the annual row less the nine-month row is the only statement of it. 2024 is left out on purpose - through that year the seller still sold part of the volume under a transition agreement and the acquirer split the product between a product-revenue row and a separate net-economic-benefit row, so there are two defensible answers and this set does not score an ambiguity it cannot state.

cases.source: The issuer sells one product. Its periodic reports carry a product revenue, net line and name the product only in prose; the XBRL instance carries that total under no product member, and the one product member in the annual instance sits on a licence milestone threshold rather than on a quarter's sales. The earnings exhibit is the document that ties the two together - "Product revenue, net consists entirely of revenue from sales of NERLYNX" - and this filing agent names it ex_973970.htm, which is the naming convention a rule matching ex99 in the filename cannot see.
